title: TAIL-2 every road to this host (authenticated)
description: GET /v1/host/roads, device credential required. The typed endpoints a pairing claim carries and this host's Tailscale identity, read fresh, so a paired app keeps its roads current (it learns the MagicDNS name at home and dials it away). Not on unauthenticated /health: that stays an anchor (host_id + fingerprint), enough to recognise the same host on another address, and never tells a stranger on the LAN where else this host can be reached.

endpoints.description: TAIL-2 P0-2: every road to this host, each with its kind. `lan` addresses first (IPv4 before IPv6), then `<host_name>.local` (`mdns`), then the MagicDNS name and the tailnet addresses (`tailnet`, 100.64.0.0/10 and fd7a:115c:a1e0::/48). An iOS client can dial a tailnet road only by its MagicDNS name (ATS); it keeps the addresses to recognise a typed 100.x as this host. A client of a core before TAIL-2 receives no `kind` and infers it.

tailnet.description: This host on its Tailscale tailnet, from `tailscale status --json`. Present only while BackendState is Running; absent without Tailscale or when it is stopped or logged out. `dns_name` is the MagicDNS name without the trailing dot (null when MagicDNS gives none).

odomo_url.description: LITE-1b C7: Odomo's https address on the tailnet, from the `tailscale serve` mapping the installer recorded (443, or 8443 when 443 is somebody else's). Absent when there is none. Authenticated documents only; never on /health.

odomo.description: LITE-1d: Odomo for a native app deciding whether to offer it. `url` is `odomo_url` again (null when this host has no front door, i.e. no Tailscale serve mapping); `push_devices` is how many of this host's web devices hold a live push subscription that the person at the computer has not switched off, with a working credential. A count only: no device ids, no endpoints. Per host, not per person (core does not know who holds a device). Absent `push_devices`: this host cannot say (no push here). The whole object is absent when the host knows neither.
